summary: To future-proof human exploration on Mars, Team Synergia proposes an interactive trip-planning map built on real surface data from rovers like Perseverance. By leveraging existing telemetry, orbital imagery, and environmental models, we ensure every new astronaut navigates complex terrains like Jezero Crater safely and efficiently. Our tool instantly calculates the safest and most energy-efficient routes—factoring in life-support limits, radiation exposure, and hidden terrain hazards—so future crews can focus on groundbreaking science rather than basic survival.
details:
What does it do?

Martian Map · INTI.NAV (Team Synergia) is an offline, browser-based decision-support tool for planning EVA walks and Perseverance-class rover drives in Jezero Crater. It computes three A* routes (shortest, lowest energy, safest) in 2D and 3D on real orbital terrain (MRO CTX/HiRISE, USGS) for 27 science targets and an astronaut or rover profile. SARA, a deterministic rule-based copilot (no AI at run time), says which route is best and why, and guides the interface with voice and subtitles. Every item is labeled as data, model or assumption.

How does it work?

Pick a target and profile → three routes are computed → overlay layers (relief, slope, USGS geology, carbonate association, thermal inertia as data; thermal stress and radiation as models) → optional HiRISE hazard check (~31 % of the map) → timeline, horizon and real Perseverance photos compared with our 3D render → crew-safety panel (round-trip oxygen, temperature, line of sight, dose, ±20 % uncertainty bracket) with editable life-support what-if parameters (team-sheet baseline, 450 L PLSS) → SARA’s verdict with the rules behind it.

Benefits:

Explainable decisions; comparison against real Perseverance traverse and photos (context, not model validation); runs offline with no install; export of a 27-target mission table and routes as CSV/GeoJSON.

What we hope to achieve:

Short term: a transparent, interactive tool to compare routes and their energy and logistics cost at Jezero. Long term: validate the models against field and mission data, add CRISM spectral maps for geological targets, HiRISE-derived roughness and a multi-stop excursion planner. Declared limits: 40 m cells miss small rocks, metabolic and thermal models are unvalidated, NOAA space weather is at 1 AU and not rescaled to Mars.

Tools used:

JavaScript and Python; React 18, three.js, Vite, esbuild, npm; Web Speech API (offline voice); Playwright, Node and Python test scripts; Python data pipelines (DTM/orthomosaic → JS); runs in Chrome/Edge on a general-purpose laptop. Development assisted by Claude (Anthropic); SARA’s illustration was generated with an AI image tool from our own design.

AI Clarifications:

Claude and Gemini were used for development support: the app, the data extraction and conversion scripts, testing, and documentation drafts.

SARA's illustration was generated with an SI image tool based on Gemini.

SARA does not use any AI models at runtime: it is a rules engine.

The team chose the sources, models, and limits, and the results were reviewed with the included tests.
